Cyclist magazine issue 179: on sale now

Cyclist magazine Issue 179, October 2026, is on sale now. Subscribe to Cyclist or buy issue 179 here.

Over 179 issues now, the Big Ride has been the centrepiece of Cyclist magazine – a long-form, photo-rich deep dive into a particularly special bike ride in a particularly special part of the world. As is the nature of these things, we’re constantly on the lookout for new locations, new roads, new adventures around which we can weave a new story to bring to you, our loyal readers.

And sometimes that can lead to the temptation to try to redefine what a ‘special bike ride’ actually is – some new way of combining human, bike, road and terrain that’s an improvement on what we’ve done before. But as our latest Big Ride in the October 2026 issue of Cyclist (available now on newsstands or from the Cyclist Store) shows, there really is no need.

We’ve made our way to the Peloponnese peninsula of mainland Greece, which greeted us with a mix of beautifully quiet roads, punchy climbs and spectacular sea views in a part of the world that’s steeped in rich history, vibrant local culture and geological marvels, and yet is a world away from the over-subscribed tourist hotspots of the Greek islands. Sun, sea and volcanoes – what’s not to like?

On the subject of history, you’ll struggle to find a richer repository of cycling history than can be seen at the Ghisallo Museum on the shores of Lake Como in Italy’s Lombardia. Its location adjacent to the famed Madonna del Ghisallo climb of Il Lombardia fame makes for the perfect two-wheeled pilgrimage to earn your right to take in the museum’s many attractions, which range from a near-70-strong collection of Giro maglia rosas to a set of post-World War 2 winner’s sashes from the Tour of Flanders and Gino Bartali’s Tour de France-winning bike from 1938. We pay a visit in our October 2026 issue and tell the bigger story behind six of the museum’s many treasures.

One man who never actually rode Il Lombardia during his two-decade pro career is Welshman Geraint Thomas – Tour de France winner, Olympic gold medallist and a key component in the all-conquering Sky/Ineos machine of the 2010s. He may now have hung up his wheels, but he’s still at the sharp end of the peloton in his new role this year as Netcompany Ineos’s director of racing. We pay Thomas a visit to talk through the challenges of his new job, from the involvement of AI in pro cycling to dealing with human tragedy within the team.

Sticking with storied names within the world of cycling, the Prova Integrale is one of those bikes that’s an icon less in terms of its sales figures or pro pedigree, and more in a ‘if you know, you know’ kind of way. A classically aesthetic marriage of the best of carbon and titanium bike engineering, hand-crafted and custom-made in Australia using techniques that include everything from 3D printing to finishing parts in a ceramic rock tumbler, it’s a worthy focus of the latest instalment in our Dream Bikes series.

Then for a complete change of scenery it’s off to Norway, where we take on an epic three-day gravel ride across the country’s mountainous interior. It’s a real rite of passage – stone trolls, ferries, reindeer stew, all-day rain, singletrack, serene lakeside tarmac… it’s all on the menu in this rugged Scandinavian riding adventure.

Elsewhere in the October 2026 issue, we have an interview with the legendary Eddy Merckx, climb the Col d’Èze of Paris-Nice fame and the character-filled Dunkery Beacon in Somerset, shine a deserved spotlight on London’s XO Cycles, which is giving ex-offenders the chance to make a new start as bike mechanics, and test out new bikes from Merida, MMR and Specialized.

There’s plenty more besides in the latest issue of Cyclist, so make sure to pick up your copy on newsstands or at the Cyclist Store or get a Cyclist magazine subscription to have every issue delivered free, straight to your door.
